The official weather of **Galicia** (Spain) in Gladys, from **MeteoGalicia**, the weather service
of the **Xunta de Galicia**: the readings of the nearest **automatic weather station** every
10 minutes, the **daily forecast** of a municipality (concello), and its **warning levels** for
today, tomorrow and the day after.

Open data: no account, no API key. This integration is not affiliated with MeteoGalicia or the
Xunta de Galicia.

## Overview

- **Two devices**: the nearest station (temperature, humidity, pressure, wind, gusts, rain: what
  the station measures) and a municipality (forecast of today and tomorrow, UV index, warning
  levels).
- **A scene trigger**, "MeteoGalicia warning level raised", as soon as MeteoGalicia raises the
  warning level of the municipality for today, tomorrow or the day after.
- **A dashboard widget** with the readings, the minimum and maximum of the coming days, the
  warning levels and the forecast of today and tomorrow.
- **Read-only**: MeteoGalicia is a data source, nothing is controlled.

## Requirements

- Gladys **5.3.0** or later.
- A place in **Galicia**: one of its 313 municipalities, within 40 km of a MeteoGalicia station.
- Your Gladys house located on the map (**Settings → Houses**), or coordinates, a station or a
  municipality typed in the configuration.
- Gladys must reach the Internet (`servizos.meteogalicia.gal`).

## Configuration

Install the integration from **Integrations → Install from GitHub** (or from the store), then
open its configuration. Every field is optional: by default the integration takes the position of
your first located house, the station nearest to it, the municipality of that station, and
refreshes every 10 minutes.

| Field                         | Use                                                                                                               |
| ----------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| House                         | The house whose position is used. Empty: the first house that has a position.                                     |
| Latitude, Longitude           | Another place than a house, for example `43.37` and `-8.40` (a comma works too). Both, or neither.                |
| Weather station               | The id of a MeteoGalicia station, for example `10157` (A Coruña). Empty: the nearest one.                         |
| Municipality                  | INE code (`15030`) or name (`A Coruña`) of the municipality for the forecast and warnings. Empty: the station's.  |
| Refresh interval              | 10, 15, 30 or 60 minutes. The stations report every 10 minutes.                                                   |
| Language of the feature names | Language of the feature names (set when the devices are created) and of the scene event texts. French by default. |

The house position is read through the Gladys `location` permission, shown when you install the
integration. It **never leaves Gladys**: the integration downloads the list of stations and picks
the nearest one itself; MeteoGalicia only receives public ids (a station, a municipality). It is
never written to the logs either.

The default municipality is the one **of the nearest station**: MeteoGalicia does not publish the
position of the municipalities. If you live near a border, type your municipality.

Then open the **Discovery** tab of the integration and add the two devices to Gladys.

## Devices

### Station

The name is "MeteoGalicia" followed by the station name. Values of the last 10-minute reading:

| Feature              | Unit | Note                                                 |
| -------------------- | ---- | ---------------------------------------------------- |
| Temperature          | °C   | Air temperature, 1.5 m                               |
| Dew point            | °C   |                                                      |
| Humidity             | %    |                                                      |
| Pressure (sea level) | hPa  | Pressure reduced to sea level, as in the forecasts   |
| Wind speed           | km/h | Mean of the 10 minutes, at 10 m (or 2 m)             |
| Wind gusts           | km/h | Strongest gust of the 10 minutes                     |
| Wind direction       | °    | Where the wind comes from: 0 = north, 90 = east      |
| Rain intensity       | mm/h | Rain of the last 10 minutes, as an hourly rate (× 6) |

A station only gets the features of what it measures (about a third of the stations have neither
wind nor pressure): a feature added once is kept, even if the station stops sending it. Only the
values MeteoGalicia marks as valid are published. A station silent for more than 3 hours is not
re-published as current.

### Municipality

The name is "MeteoGalicia" followed by the municipality name. Its daily forecast and the highest
warning level announced for it:

| Feature                | Unit   | Note                                                             |
| ---------------------- | ------ | ---------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Weather today          | text   | Most representative sky of the day, e.g. "Light showers"         |
| Minimum today          | °C     | Galician days (Europe/Madrid)                                    |
| Maximum today          | °C     |                                                                  |
| UV index today         | index  | Highest UV index forecast                                        |
| Weather tomorrow       | text   |                                                                  |
| Minimum tomorrow       | °C     |                                                                  |
| Maximum tomorrow       | °C     |                                                                  |
| Warning level today    | 0 to 3 | Highest level of the day: 0 none, 1 yellow, 2 orange, 3 red      |
| Warning level tomorrow | 0 to 3 |                                                                  |
| Weather warnings       | text   | The days with a warning, e.g. "Today: Yellow · Tomorrow: Orange" |

The levels are the highest of the whole day for the municipality, whatever the phenomenon (wind,
rain, coastal event, snow, heat…), as MeteoGalicia publishes them per municipality.

## Widget

**MeteoGalicia weather** shows, in the language and units of the dashboard:

- the municipality name (as named in Gladys), then the temperature, humidity, wind and gusts of
  the station;
- the minimum and maximum of the coming days (up to 4);
- the warning level of each day that has one, or a green "None" line;
- the weather of today and tomorrow, with their minimum, maximum and chance of rain;
- the source and the time of the reading.

The **Blocks to hide** setting hides the station readings, the chart, the warning levels or the
forecast of today and tomorrow.

## Scene trigger

**MeteoGalicia warning level raised** fires when the highest warning level of the municipality
rises for a day (today, tomorrow or the day after): from none to yellow, from yellow to orange…
Once per day and per level, as soon as it is announced (a level that goes down and back up the same day does not fire again). A restart does not fire it again, nor the
next day when "tomorrow" becomes "today". The very first start (and the first start after a
change of municipality) only takes note of the levels already announced.

Filters (empty = any): **Levels** (yellow, orange, red) and **Days** (today, tomorrow, day after
tomorrow).

Information passed to the scene actions: level, level (1 to 3), level key, day, day key, date,
raised from a lower warning, municipality. For example, a message: `MeteoGalicia:
\{\{triggerEvent.data.level_label\}\} warning \{\{triggerEvent.data.day_label\}\} in
\{\{triggerEvent.data.concello\}\}`.

## Configuration actions

- **List the nearest stations**: the 8 stations nearest to the place, with their id,
  municipality, altitude and distance. Copy an id into "Weather station" to choose another one (a
  station in the valley often fits better than a nearer one on a summit).
- **Check the connection**: reads every source now and says what answered: the station
  temperature and its time, the municipality of the forecast, today's warning level. Shown in red
  if a source failed.

## Scene examples

- **Storm coming**: trigger "MeteoGalicia warning level raised", levels "Orange" and "Red" → close
  the shutters, retract the awning, send a message with the day.
- **Strong sun**: every day at 10:00, if "UV index today" is greater than or equal to 6 → remind
  to put sunscreen on the children.
- **Frost tomorrow**: every evening at 20:00, if "Minimum tomorrow" is below 1 °C → notify to
  protect the plants and the windshield.

## Troubleshooting

- **"No location"**: no house has a position. Place your house on the map in **Settings →
  Houses**, or type coordinates, a station or a municipality.
- **"Outside Galicia"**: the place is more than 40 km away from every MeteoGalicia station. Type a
  station or a municipality to use the integration anyway.
- **"Not among the 313"**: the municipality typed is unknown. Type its 5-digit INE code (for
  example `15078` for Santiago de Compostela) or its name.
- **"MeteoGalicia does not answer"**: Gladys cannot reach `servizos.meteogalicia.gal`; the values
  are updated when it is back. The logs say which source fails, once, and when it works again.
- **A feature is missing on the station**: the station does not measure it. Choose another
  station with **List the nearest stations**.
- **More details**: set the `LOG_LEVEL` variable of the container to `debug`.

## Limits

- **Data**: open data of MeteoGalicia (Xunta de Galicia), reused with the mention of the source
  ("Source: MeteoGalicia – Xunta de Galicia", shown by the widget).
- **Requests**: about 13 an hour at the default pace (station and warning levels every refresh,
  forecast once an hour, the lists of stations and municipalities once a day). The stations report
  every 10 minutes: a faster pace would read nothing new.
- The warnings are the **highest level per day and municipality**: the phenomenon (wind, rain,
  coast…) and the exact hours are not published by this service.
- The forecast is daily (today and the next 2 or 3 days); no hourly forecast. Solar radiation and
  soil temperatures are not published as features (no matching unit in Gladys).
- One station and one municipality per installation.
- The feature names are set when the devices are created: changing the language later does not
  rename them.
- Developed without access to an official specification of every service: MeteoGalicia may change
  them without notice. Feedback welcome.

## Configuration settings

These are the settings MeteoGalicia asks for in its configuration screen in Gladys.

| Setting | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| MeteoGalicia | `section` | No | Open data of MeteoGalicia, the weather service of the Xunta de Galicia: no account, no key. By default, the integration uses the position of your first Gladys house: the nearest automatic station, and the forecast and warning levels of that station's municipality. Not affiliated with MeteoGalicia or the Xunta de Galicia. |
| House | `select` | No | The house whose position is used. Empty: the first house with a position. |
| Latitude (optional) | `string` | No | To use another place than a house. Takes precedence over the house. |
| Longitude (optional) | `string` | No |  |
| Weather station (optional) | `string` | No | Id of a MeteoGalicia automatic station. Empty: the nearest one. The action below lists them. |
| Municipality (optional) | `string` | No | INE code or name of a Galician municipality, for the forecast and warnings. Empty: that of the station. |
| Refresh interval | `select` | No | The stations report every 10 minutes. |
| Language of the feature names | `select` | No | Used when the devices are created, and for the scene event texts. |

## How to install MeteoGalicia in Gladys

1. In Gladys, open **Integrations**: MeteoGalicia appears in the catalog, next to the native integrations, with a community badge.
2. Click **Install**. Gladys pulls the Docker image (`ghcr.io/guim31/gladys-meteogalicia:1.0.0`), starts it in a sandbox isolated from the core, and generates the integration's interface (devices, discovery and configuration).
3. Open the **Configuration** screen of the integration, fill in the settings, and save.
4. You can also install it directly from its repository URL: [https://github.com/guim31/gladys-meteogalicia](https://github.com/guim31/gladys-meteogalicia).

MeteoGalicia requires Gladys `>=5.3.0`. The catalog inside Gladys refreshes every hour, so a new version becomes available at most one hour after its release.

Not running Gladys yet? It is free and open source: [follow the installation guide](/docs/) to get started.

## About external integrations

MeteoGalicia is an **external integration**: a community integration packaged as a Docker container and published on GitHub, that Gladys installs in one click and runs in a sandbox isolated from its core.
